data.title: Captain's Log 45.7.21
data.author: Captain Helena Zhao
data.excerpt: There is nothing to salvage. Only debris, salt, and the taste of a vanished system.
data.body:
This is Captain Helena Zhao of the salvage vessel Second Breakfast.

Miranda's primary sun went supernova without warning. Inner planets vaporized. Outer planetoids were thrown into cold darkness. We entered the debris field expecting a graveyard and found something worse: a silence that feels arranged.

Some say you can still taste celery salt in the dust. I laughed when I first heard it. I am not laughing now.

data.title: Crew Medical Watch
data.author: Dr. Imani Vale
data.excerpt: Headaches, nausea, deja vu. Nobody wants to say the symptoms out loud twice.
data.body:
Three crew reported headaches after handling drone returns from the debris field. Two described dreams of a bar they have never visited. One woke up repeating a drink order in a voice he claims was not his own.

No abnormalities on scans. No fever. No infection. The fear is the only thing progressing.

Recommendation: limit direct exposure to recovered signal caches, especially any reference to a Bloody Mary and any insistence on pickle prohibition.

data.title: Private Memorandum
data.author: First Officer Soren Pike
data.excerpt: The captain looks composed until someone mentions drinks, dreams, or card players.
data.body:
The captain has not slept properly in eleven cycles. She denies it, but the evidence is in the way she freezes whenever recovered transcripts mention the saloon.

Twice now she has asked whether anyone else has seen three old men through the bridge glass. There was nobody there. On the second occasion she also asked whether the ship kept a safe for paper records.

It does now.

data.title: Vault Fragment: Recipe Lockbox
data.author: Recovered hardcopy, access restricted
data.excerpt: The page keeps moving. The phrase keeps returning. The paper smells faintly of tomato, iron, and smoke.
data.body:
Cross-reference from the mechanical observer and the old man's account suggests a causality nexus formed around a drink completed at the instant of Miranda's destruction.

Hardcopy fragment secured in captain's vault after digital copies exhibited instability. Crew instructed not to vocalize the activation phrase aloud.

Fragment note: "Bloody Mary, no pickles, make it a double."

If this page is found outside the safe again, burn it and do not discuss the ash.

data.title: Engineering Memo 8.15
data.author: Chief Engineer Mara Quill
data.excerpt: The ship is humming in sympathy with transmissions that should no longer exist.
data.body:
Reactor output remains nominal, but the harmonic drift is wrong. Every time we pass through a dense pocket of Miranda ash, the engine room resonates with carrier bands matching the dead system's final RF burst.

It sounds like traffic stacked above an atmosphere that is no longer there. Queue chatter. Clearance loops. Repeated holds.

I have shut down three relays and the sound still comes through the deck.

data.title: Quarantine Bay Slip
data.author: Dr. Imani Vale
data.excerpt: The sleepers are not dead. The ship still refuses to classify them as living.
data.body:
We sealed three crew inside the aft medbay after the Miranda ash dreams escalated into waking fugues. They answer to their names, but only after a delay, as if translating from somewhere farther away.

Their body temperatures fall whenever the Bloody Mary phrase is spoken near the pods. The glass frosts from the inside first.

I have ordered the quarantine lamps to stay red until somebody can explain why the EEG spikes match the ship's own telemetry.

data.title: Mess Ledger Addendum
data.author: Steward Callum Reef
data.excerpt: We ran out of clean water before we ran out of stories about the bar.
data.body:
Nobody eats in the mess unless the speakers are playing static. If the channels are quiet, people start hearing the card table again.

The bowls rattle whenever we cross a dense ash current. Plates slide toward the aft corridor as if the ship itself leans toward Miranda.

I locked the pantry and still found celery salt on the floor this morning.

data.title: Brig Confession
data.author: Unnamed detainee
data.excerpt: I was not trying to open the safe. I was trying to put the page back.
data.body:
They locked me in the brig because I kept leaving the corridor at night and waking up near the captain's office with soot under my nails.

The truth is smaller and worse: every time I close my eyes, I can hear a voice asking me to return a recipe card to its proper era.

The bars hum when the engines drift. The hum knows my name.

data.title: Archive Index: Recovered Echoes
data.author: Signal Archivist Nila Serrin
data.excerpt: Each copied transcript diverges the second time it is opened.
data.body:
The upper archive is no longer storing files. It is growing variants.

Open one Miranda transcript and you receive an account. Open it again and the witness order changes. Open it a third time and there is a fourth witness seated at the table.

I moved the worst logs to the upper stacks and disconnected them from the main grid. The lights in this gallery still blink in answers.
